To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
conversational user interfaces are attractive to customers for the use cases: “Product Search and Selection”, “Order Status and Tracking” and “Customer Service”.
conversational commerce is a promising field for online retailers.
conversational user interfaces are a must-be for all customer groups and that the use of messaging services is attractive for the younger and voice assistants for the older customer groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: 1.
the following research questions: Which use case groups and customer segments are relevant for conversational user interfaces in online shops?
the question of which use cases of conversational user interfaces are attractive to customers and how they influence customers’ satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no “one-size-fits-all” solution.
there are no must-be use cases and no customer segments that are more attractive than others.
conversational user interfaces in general have the potential to improve customer satisfaction, but that the use cases have to be designed and implemented in an appropriate way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use cases for messaging services and voice assistant have a high relevance for customers.
there are different use cases for messaging services and for voice assistants.
the use of messaging service and voice assistant for online shops is not a must-be for customers and the use cases are attractive only for a specific customer segment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use cases are categorized into 5 segments: Must-Be, Must-Have, One-Dimensional, Attractive and Unattractive.
the customer satisfaction is not influenced by the use case itself.
the use cases for messaging services and voice assistant differ.
